newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - British retailer Sears profits slide.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - British retailer Sears profits slide.

text.p: British retailer Sears, under pressure to turn around its sprawling retail empire, on Tuesday saw half year profits virtually wiped out by provisions for rationalising its British Shoe unit.
But Sears, whose business spans shoes, womens fashion and London's Selfridges department store, said the reorganisation was complete and the group could now start making progress.
Chief executive Liam Strong said he believed the company had put the steps in place to achieve a better performance.
"We are looking for a steady improvement in performance from now on," he said in a telephone interview.
Investors, braced for dismal first half results, were mildly encouraged by the figures, which were at the top of market expectations.
"The trading statement is not bad and things seem to be on an improving trend," said one retail analyst.
Sears' shares rose 1.5 pence to 98.5 pence.
Pretax profit including the provisions was 2.5 million pounds ($3.89 million) against 29.9 million last time.
Profits excluding provisions rose 3.7 percent to 28 million pounds. Sales from ongoing businesses were up 7.9 percent to 843.1 million pounds.
Gains in womens fashion and the flagship Selfridges store were overshadowed by poor trading in home shopping and shoes.
Sears has struggled to streamline its stores to revive profits but radical pruning over the past four years has been slow to restore growth.

And an upturn in consumer confidence -- the feelgood factor -- which has helped turn around other stores such as Kingfisher Plc, has yet to rescue Sears, still one of the poorest performers in the retail sector.
Angry shareholders called in June for chief executive Strong to quit because of lack of progress. But Strong, taken on four years ago to revamp the company, said his future was not in question.
His efforts to ditch parts of British Shoe were hampered this year when stores sold to retailer Facia had to be taken back after Facia collapsed in June.
Strong said Sears had sold 149 of the 379 stores it had to take back, 85 were under offer and 145 were still for sale.
The company set aside 32.5 million pounds to cover the cost of property disposals and debts owed to Sears by Facia.
The charge was partly offset by the release of 7.5 million pounds in provisions held over from the previous year, making a net new provision of 25.0 million pounds.
Footwear sales fell 4.6 percent in the first half and profits slid to 600,000 pounds from two million.

Selfridges was again the star performer with profits up by 21.8 percent to 13.4 million pounds. The group plans to open a Selfridges in Manchester in 1998 and may open another three or four regional stores by the year 2000.
Selfridges in London's main shopping district, Oxford Street, could gain also an extra 200,000 square feet of space if current development plans go ahead.
Freemans, the mail order business, saw sales fall 6.5 percent to 237.0 million pounds, but there has been some recovery so far in the second half.
